Claim (our original wording): Hand hygiene observation uses five moments: (1) Before touching a patient, (2) Before a clean/aseptic procedure, (3) After body fluid exposure risk, (4) After touching a patient, and (5) After touching patient surroundings.
Source: WHO Hand Hygiene Technical Reference Manual 2009 [TRM]
Expected section/topic: Five moments for hand hygiene concept & indications
Verification status: Not yet verified against source text – check during local IPC lead review
Notes: Original wording only; no WHO graphics bundled.

Claim (our original wording): When one or more hand hygiene indications (moments) occur together at the same time between care tasks, they are recorded as ONE single hand hygiene opportunity and counted once.
Source: WHO Hand Hygiene Technical Reference Manual 2009 [TRM]
Expected section/topic: Definition of opportunity vs. indication during direct observation
Verification status: Not yet verified against source text – check during local IPC lead review
Notes: Prevents double-counting transition between patients.

Claim (our original wording): Hand hygiene adherence (compliance) percentage is calculated as 100 multiplied by total positive actions (hand rub + handwash) divided by total opportunities.
Source: WHO Hand Hygiene Technical Reference Manual 2009 [TRM]
Expected section/topic: Compliance calculation formula
Verification status: Not yet verified against source text – check during local IPC lead review
Notes: Denominator is opportunities, not indications.

Claim (our original wording): Each observed opportunity has exactly one recorded action outcome: alcohol-based hand rub, handwashing with soap and water, or missed (counted as not performed).
Source: WHO Hand Hygiene Technical Reference Manual 2009 [TRM]
Expected section/topic: Recording hand hygiene actions (rub, wash, missed)
Verification status: Not yet verified against source text – check during local IPC lead review

Claim (our original wording): Multiple observation sessions are combined by summing action counts and opportunity counts first before calculating adherence, never by averaging session percentages.

Verification status: Kit design choice (mathematical rule)

Claim (our original wording): Adherence is always displayed with numerator and denominator counts ('X of Y opportunities, Z%'), shows 'No observations' when Y = 0, and avoids misleading 0% or 100% rounding on non-extreme values.
